chapter: Trent's band: Texas, St. Louis and the road east
title: Brown Hotel in Louisville and Lexington in 1927-28
summary: They play the Brown Hotel for a few nights and spend months in a fine Lexington spot for whites; a song is published there.

story.theme_name: Life on the road: touring bands, buses and one-nighters
story.community_name: Life on the road: buses, trains and one-nighters

blocks.x: DID YOU PLAY THE BROWN HOTEL IN LOUISVILLE.
We played the Brown Hotel in Louisville, yes.
WAS THAT A STEADY JOB.
No, we only played there for about three or four nights.
OH YEAH.
It was located at the end of a street. It was like a dead end you walked right into the hotel. I remember the Brown, yeah, it was in Louisville.
STUFF WAS WITH THE BAND ALREADY.
Yeah, that was 1928 I think.
THAT WAS ABOUT THE TIME. WHO WAS ON THE BOAT?
Stuff was on the boat. It was 1927 when we were on the boat, because this number was published in Lexington, Kentucky. We were playing in Lexington, Kentucky.
WAS THERE A HOTEL THERE?
No, but it was a fine spot there, we stayed for about two or three months in Lexington.
IT DIDN'T SEEM LIKE THERE WOULD BE THAT MUCH BUSINESS.
Yes, it was. It was right downtown, a fine place.
I was talking to a guy about a month ago, he was from Lexington, he said that the only thing wrong with Trent's band was that we couldn't go in there and play.
OH YEAH. YOU MEAN PLAYING JUST FOR WHITES. THERE WERE SOME GUYS FROM HERE WHO WERE FROM LEXINGTON.
Who live here now, yeah.
TRY TO REMEMBER THE NAMES OF THE PLACES WHEN YOU GET TOGETHER AGAIN.
Yeah, he would remember the place, I can call him up and find out.
CALL HIM AND FIND OUT.
He was a very good friend of Al Bernie. I remember meeting him at Al's party from (inaudible) of the place and I've forgotten the name.
WHERE WOULD YOU HAVE GONE IN 1928?
That's 1928.
THIS SONG WAS PUBLISHED IN 1928.
Right.
LEON MOSLEY "All My Dreams Were Yesterday."
Right.
DO YOU HAVE ANY COPIES OF THAT?
No.
1800 ROCK STREET, LITTLE ROCK.
That's my home spot.
